key_insight: A transfer principle converts continuous elliptic Carleman estimates into mesh-uniform discrete estimates without added stabilization, with radial-weight parameters satisfying s ≤ ch^(-4/5).
engineering_relevance: The framework supports stability analysis for finite-element and finite-difference inverse boundary problems relevant to reconstructing spatially varying material properties.
method: Construct a shifted continuous problem whose Galerkin solution reproduces the prescribed discrete state.
Use weighted approximation to transfer continuous estimates to the discrete operator.
Apply the estimates to discrete Calderón recovery from independently prescribed, possibly disjoint boundary patches.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical verification for piecewise affine FEM with consistent or lumped mass and Cartesian finite differences, yielding a single logarithmic data term and an O(h^(1/2)) mesh remainder.
watch_item: The inverse stability result assumes dimension d ≥ 3, potential agreement near the boundary, and uniformly stable discrete Dirichlet problems.
paper_title: A Transfer Principle for Elliptic Carleman Estimates: Application to Discrete Calderón Stability
